messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

The user wants to find libraries in three cities with certain facilities. We need to call the function multiple times. The function signature: public_library_find_nearby takes location string and facilities which can be one of the enumerated values? Wait: facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]; So facilities is a union type? Actually it's a union of string or array? It says "Facilities and sections in public library." The type is "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]; That seems ambiguous. But likely we pass an array of strings? The example says "Cafe"[] meaning array of Cafe? Might be mis-specified. But we can pass an array of strings: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"] etc.

We need to call function thrice:

1. location: "New York, NY" facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"]
2. location: "Los Angeles, CA" facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"]
3. location: "Chicago, IL" facilities: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"]

But the function expects a single facility? Actually it might accept array. We'll pass array.

We'll produce calls accordingly.
